summary: MIT is need-blind for every applicant on earth and meets 100% of demonstrated need for four years. From 2025–26, students from families earning under $200,000 attend tuition-free, and families under $100,000 are not expected to contribute at all.
covers: Need-blind admission for all applicants, domestic and international.
100% of demonstrated need met for the full length of your degree.
Family income under $200,000 (with typical assets): no tuition. Under $100,000: no family contribution towards the cost of attendance.
eligibility: First-year applicants from any country applying to MIT's undergraduate programme.
MIT assesses need from your family's income and assets; typical assets are assumed in the published thresholds.
how_to_apply: Apply through MIT's own application portal (MIT does not use the Common App).
Early Action closes on 1 November; Regular Action closes in early January (4 January in the latest cycle).
Submit the financial aid application separately: by 30 November for Early Action applicants and by 15 February for Regular Action.
Complete MIT's essays and interview if one is offered in your country.
watch_out: Aid deadlines differ from admission deadlines — put both in your calendar.
Early Action at MIT is non-binding, so applying early costs you nothing.
Very few international students are admitted each year; apply to other need-blind and full-need colleges too.

sources.title: MIT Admissions — Undergraduates with family income below $200,000 can attend tuition-free
